ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, fold side AD of the rectangle so that point D falls on point F on side BC. If $ AB=8\,cm$ and $BC=10\,cm$, what is the length of EC in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
hence AB=CD=8cm, AD=BC=10cm, $\angle$B=$\angle$C=$90^\circ$,\\
By the property of folding: AF=AD=10cm, DE=EF,\\
In $\triangle$ABF, BF=$\sqrt{AF^{2}-AB^{2}}=6cm$,\\
thus CF=BC-BF=4cm,\\
Let EC=x, then DE=EF=8-x,\\
In $\triangle$EFC, since EF$^{2}$=EC$^{2}$+CF$^{2}$,\\
thus (8-x)$^{2}$=x$^{2}$+4$^{2}$,\\
thus x=\boxed{3}cm,

By the property of folding, AF = AD = 10 cm and DE = EF. In \triangle ABF, BF = \sqrt{AF^2 - AB^2} = 6 cm, so CF = BC - BF = 4 cm. Let EC = x, then DE = EF = 8 - x. In \triangle EFC, EF^2 = EC^2 + CF^2, so (8 - x)^2 = x^2 + 4^2, thus x = 3 cm.

By the property of folding, AF = AD = 10 cm and DE = EF. In \triangle ABF, BF = \sqrt{AF^2 - AB^2} = 6 cm, so CF = BC - BF = 4 cm. Let EC = x, then DE = EF = 8 - x. ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point F is on the bottom side BC, and point E is on the right side CD. There is a crease AE in the figure; a dashed line connects A to E. After folding, point D falls on point F on BC, and line segments AF and EF are formed. Reasoning: In rectangle ABCD, AB = CD = 8 cm, BC = AD = 10 cm. Because D falls to F when folding, and A remains unchanged on the crease, AF = AD = 10 cm; at the same time, E is on the crease, and the corresponding line segments before and after folding satisfy DE = EF. In right triangle ABF, AB = 8, AF = 10, so BF = sqrt(10^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(36) = 6 cm. Therefore CF = BC - BF = 10 - 6 = 4 cm. Let EC = x, then DE = CD - EC = 8 - x, so EF = 8 - x. In right triangle EFC, EF^2 = EC^2 + CF^2, namely (8 - x)^2 = x^2 + 4^2. Expanding gives 64 - 16x + x^2 = x^2 + 16, so 48 = 16x, x = 3. Therefore EC = 3 cm.
